data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Japan factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Japan performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results relate to trends since 2018 and earlier cycles. The assessment uses two hour-long tests per student with different subject combinations, plus a student background questionnaire and a school principal questionnaire; the factsheet reports mean performance, proficiency-level shares (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and subgroup patterns such as socioeconomic gradients and gender differences. For Japan, 5,760 students in 182 schools completed the assessment, representing about 1,021,400 15-year-olds. The factsheet also notes COVID-19-related disruptions and indicates that Japan met PISA quality standards for reporting. No predictive or machine-learning modeling is conducted in this document; it is a descriptive reporting of PISA results using OECD’s published database tables and uncertainty intervals.
